title.rendered: Talent is entry fee, not ticket to success — King Ereso

content.rendered:
Lagos-based contemporary artist, King Ereso, has attributed his growing international recognition to faith, discipline and a long-term approach to building his career, saying talent alone is not enough to succeed on the global stage.

Speaking in an interview with Saturday Beats, the artist, whose works are currently displayed at the Four Seasons Hotel in Singapore, and who is exclusively represented in Asia by Yang Gallery, said years of consistent effort prepared him for international opportunities.

He said, “Talent is just the starting point. It is the entry fee, not the ticket,” he said, adding that his Christian faith had been central to his artistic journey.

Ereso noted that he remained committed to refining his craft by focusing on self-improvement rather than comparing himself with other artists.

Reflecting on his artistic style, he explained that his works draw heavily from his Edo heritage and the history of the Benin Kingdom, while incorporating Ankara-inspired fashion and his signature teal palette.

He maintained that staying authentic to his Nigerian roots has enabled his art to resonate with collectors across Asia, Europe and the Americas.

“I have never seen those two things as opposites. Being deeply rooted in who I am is exactly what makes the work feel universal,” he said.

The artist also dismissed suggestions that recurring elements such as teal and ankara function merely as symbols, describing them instead as deeply personal expressions of his identity.

According to him, his fascination with patterns, textiles and fashion naturally finds expression in his paintings, sculptures and other creative works.

Speaking on his career development, Ereso credited Lagos-based Kontroversial Studios for helping him adopt a structured, long-term strategy rather than chasing visibility.

He said the management company allowed him to focus on creating art while building relationships with galleries and institutions capable of sustaining his career.

“Hustle without strategy is just exhaustion,” he said, adding that a strong management structure had given him the freedom to take creative risks.

He expressed optimism about future collaborations with leading global luxury brands, saying the partnership had reinforced his belief that Nigerian contemporary art belongs on the world’s biggest platforms.

Beyond painting, the artist revealed that he has long been involved in graphic design, sculpture, fashion and character development.

He said his original character, Dave, which he began developing in 2023, was conceived as a global storytelling universe spanning animation and episodic content.

According to him, these creative disciplines have always existed alongside his painting practice rather than representing a new direction.

“The canvas is the foundation, absolutely. But to limit myself to one medium would be to silence parts of myself,” he said.

Addressing young Nigerian artists, Ereso encouraged them to reject limiting beliefs about international success.
